heading: INT. UNCLAIMED UMBRELLA DEPOT - TRANSIT LOST PROPERTY BASEMENT - DAY

units.text: INT. UNCLAIMED UMBRELLA DEPOT - TRANSIT LOST PROPERTY BASEMENT - DAY
Eleven thousand umbrellas hang from the ceiling pipes like a congregation of sleeping bats, each tagged, each waiting for an owner who stopped believing in them years ago.
Fluorescent tubes hum a half-tone flat.
DELPHINE OKONKWO-REYES (50s, silver bob, a cardigan buttoned one hole too high) pours tea from a thermos into five paper cups with the care of a priestess.
The cups match.
Nothing else in the room does.
BARNABY QUILL (40s, rumpled, a man who irons only the collar) sits on an overturned crate, polishing a single brass umbrella handle that no one has asked him to polish.
TOMOKO ARAI (30s, sharp-eyed, hair pinned with a pencil) tallies index cards into stacks.
The stacks are very straight.
GUS PRZYBYLSKI (60s, broad, a retired bus driver who took this job "for the quiet") winds a wall clock that has not told the right time since March.
MEERA SUNDARAM-HOLT (20s, the newest, lanyard still stiff) holds her cup with both hands and does not drink.
Delphine sets the thermos down.
Squares it to the table edge.
Smiles at nobody.
Lovely to have everyone down here at once. Truly. It's been, what, since the Christmas lunch?
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: The lunch was in the stairwell.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Cozy, though.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Four hundred and twelve intake forms this month. Up nine percent.
units.name: TOMOKO

units.text: Nine! Wonderful. People keep losing things. It's the one thing we can count on.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Count on. Right.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Gus, you look well. Is that a new coat?
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Nineteen ninety-eight.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Timeless.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Is there an agenda?
units.name: MEERA

units.text: Agenda. No, no. Just a catch-up. We never catch up.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Delphine, the elevator has been shut off since eight this morning.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Maintenance.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Nobody told maintenance, I asked.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Then it's a surprise maintenance.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: I've never seen the upstairs door locked from the outside.
units.name: TOMOKO

units.text: Draughts. The building has draughts.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Nice tea.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Oolong. Someone brought it in. I think it was left behind by a customer and nobody claimed it, so, technically, ours.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: That's in the policy. Ninety days, then disposal or reassignment.
units.name: MEERA

units.text: Meera knows the policy. Meera is going to go far.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Is that a promotion?
units.name: MEERA

units.text: It's an observation.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: What's in the folder?
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Which folder?
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: The one under the thermos. Cream. Five tabs. Five names.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Those are the, ah, the umbrella reconciliation sheets.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: I do the reconciliation sheets. They're green.
units.name: TOMOKO

units.text: New format.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: They've got our names on the tabs.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Because we're all, you know, reconciled.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Delphine.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Barnaby.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: How long have you had the cups?
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: What?
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Five matching cups. This building has never owned five matching anything.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: I wanted it to be nice.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: For what?
units.name: TOMOKO

units.text: For whatever it is.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: Ninety days, then disposal or reassignment.
units.name: GUS

units.text: I said that.
units.name: MEERA

units.text: I know you did, love.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Delphine slides the cream folder across the table.
Her hand does not shake.
Her thermos lid, left unscrewed, rolls in a slow half-circle and drops off the edge.
Nobody picks it up.
Above them, one umbrella turns on its hook in air from no vent, and every tag along the pipe begins, softly, to tick.
